subject: Strategic step-up earnout & volume guard for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solsticetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-28T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — proposing a step-up earnout + volume guard

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion, I pulled together a proposal that aims to: 1) preserve SolsticeTech's 12-month unit economics through a short-term price hold, 2) let you scale capacity with minimal operational friction, and 3) create a performance-aligned step-up that returns credits if additional usage thresholds are met (we call this an "earnout").

High-level summary (see attached renewal-term-draft.pdf and pricing grid):
- Year 1: 10% list discount floor with a 3-month price hold on current committed rates (gives breathing room for your Q1 migration).
- Step-up earnout (Year 2): If SolsticeTech increases commit by >= 40% in the first 6 months of Year 2, Redwood will remit a one-time credit equal to 6% of additional committed spend (applied as account credit).
- Volume guard: If usage drops below 85% of committed baseline in any given quarter, price protection applies for that quarter (no automatic rate increase, up to 2 quarters).
- Ops/Delivery: Dedicated onboarding slot guaranteed within 30 days of signature; optional burst pool for seasonal spikes.

I included a conservative pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx) and a short-term draft (renewal-term-draft.pdf). This structure is intentionally tradeable — we can tighten the earnout trigger, convert part of the credit into invoice deferral, or add a true-up cadence.

Can you confirm whether procurement wants the price-hold window to start on signature or the first day of the next billing cycle? Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with Evan and the procurement team to align.

Quick ask: If this looks directionally OK, can you share the RFQ/PO format the procurement team prefers so we can pass a clean DocuSign?

Thanks,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Commercial
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solsticetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@solsticetech.com>, procurement@solsticetech.com
Date: 2027-11-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — proposing a step-up earnout + volume guard

Marissa,

Appreciate the clear summary — this is the kind of structure our finance and procurement teams like to review. Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) Procurement wants the price-hold to start on the first day of the next billing cycle (we run fiscal cycles start of month).
2) On the earnout credit: finance prefers the credit be split — 50% as immediate account credit, 50% paid as a quarterly rebate after usage is validated. They also want a clean definition of how "additional committed spend" is measured (baseline months and excluded pilot projects).

I've attached a short RFQ from procurement (procurement-rfq.pdf) — it lists mandatory contract terms (audit access, data residency note, indemnity caps) and preferred PO format. Evan will help coordinate.

Can you: 1) update the draft to reflect price-hold start date flexibility, and 2) propose language for the split credit + measurement window?

Samira
Director, Cloud Ops
SolsticeTech
samira.khan@solsticetech.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solsticetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@redwood.com>, procurement@solsticetech.com
Date: 2027-11-05T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — proposing a step-up earnout + volume guard

Thanks, Samira — this is helpful. We've updated the approach and I captured updated language below (will push a redline to the draft once you confirm).

Proposed adjustments: 
- Price-hold trigger: Start date flexible to either signature date OR first day of next billing cycle (Solstice to indicate preference on signature page).
- Earnout credit mechanics: "Additional committed spend" is measured as the incremental committed $ over the 12-month rolling baseline defined as the 12 months prior to the new term start, excluding sandbox/pilot projects with prior written notice.
  - Credit split: 50% applied as immediate account credit upon manifesting the increased commit; 50% paid as quarterly rebate after usage verification (3-month verification window; Redwood to provide token-level usage logs).
- Validation: Redwood will provide token-level usage report and a reconciled invoice feed within 30 days of quarter close for rebate reconciliation.

Operational notes: we can include a one-time implementation credit (up to $30k) if Solstice commits to onboarding > 2 new teams within 90 days. This is discretionary and tied to adoption milestones (easy to remove if procurement prefers).

Next steps: if this language looks directionally good, I can share a redline with the two options for price-hold start and a sample PO/DocuSign flow.

Cheers,
Marissa

On a separate note, marking Ben/Markus for internal alignment on the implementation credit — Ben, can you confirm budget authority for a $30k adoption credit?
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — budget sign-off and concession guidance

Marissa — quick internal note (forwarding thread to my inbox for record).

We have room for a controlled concession: approve up to $30k one-time adoption credit, but tie it to clear, short milestones and a clawback if adoption not met by day 120. For the earnout split, OK to do 50/50 but require Redwood ops SLA clause for the usage reporting (30 days, agreed schema).

If procurement pushes to move the entire credit to invoice deferral, push back — split credit is preferable to preserve cash flow. If they insist on deferral, trade it for a slightly higher Year 1 discount (max incremental 1.5%).

I'll be available for the procurement call next Tuesday.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solsticetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@solsticetech.com>, procurement@solsticetech.com
Date: 2027-11-16T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — proposing a step-up earnout + volume guard

Marissa, Ben — thanks for the clarity and internal alignment. Procurement reviewed and is OK with the split-credit approach and the verification cadence as long as Redwood provides the token-level usage export within 30 days (we'll include an SLA line in the PO). They want the price-hold to start on the first day of the next billing cycle.

We will proceed in principle on the terms below:
- Year 1 price-hold starting first day of next billing cycle
- Earnout: 50% account credit / 50% post-verified quarterly rebate
- One-time $30k adoption credit tied to 2-team onboarding milestone; clawback if adoption not reached by day 120

Please send a redline and a DocuSign packet (PO + contract addendum). I've copied procurement to provide the PO template; Evan will assemble the internal approvals.

Samira

--
Samira Khan
Director, Cloud Ops
SolsticeTech
